title: Embeddings & Rerank compatibility parity — error mapping and pagination migration playbook
creator: Marcus Li
description: Goal: implement a compatibility layer that provides parity between legacy embeddings/rerank endpoints and the unified embeddings+rerank API surface. This ticket captures the engineering playbook to map legacy HTTP error codes, standardize pagination semantics (cursor vs page tokens), enforce deterministic idempotency, and provide graceful fallbacks for downstream clients. Scope: error mapping, pagination contract, request/response transformation, integration tests, migration rollout, and monitoring dashboards. Out of scope: model-level score changes or changes to reranker heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy client requests to /v1/legacy/embeddings and /v1/legacy/rerank routed through compatibility layer return equivalent success responses for canonical inputs
HTTP error mappings documented and implemented: legacy 4xx/5xx -> unified error types + machine-readable error codes
Pagination semantics: legacy cursor-based pagination can be translated to unified page_token and back without loss of ordering or duplicates
Idempotency: duplicate request detection honors legacy idempotency headers and new idempotency-token header
Integration test suite with representative datasets passes in CI and on the staging compatibility cluster
Canary rollout succeeds with automated rollback on defined SLO regressions (latency, error rate, correctness)
Migration playbook and client-sample snippets published in internal Confluence and linked from the release notes
design_decisions: Map legacy 429 -> unified RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with 'retry_after' in response body (ms). Keep HTTP 429 as transport code for immediate rate signalling.
Convert legacy 400-series typed errors into a structured 'error.code' string (eg. ERR_INVALID_CURSOR, ERR_UNSUPPORTED_EMBED_DIM) and include legacy_error_code numeric field for audit

Use opaque base64 page_token for unified API. Compatibility layer will accept legacy cursor strings and translate them to base64-encoded page_tokens. Back-translation supported for read-after-write ordering guarantees.
For rerank cursor semantics where clients relied on stable ranking offsets, include 'cursor_anchor' metadata in page_token to ensure deterministic continuation despite sharding

Favor non-breaking transforms in the compatibility layer: do not alter embedding vectors or reranker scores except to re-encode numeric formats (float32 -> float32 JSON), or adjust trailing zeros in serialized vectors to maintain byte-for-byte equivalence where possible
implementation_notes: Create compatibility proxy service (compat-proxy) sitting in front of unified embeddings/rerank handlers. Proxy will be feature-flagged per-route.
Error translation module: canonicalize all internal errors to a compatibility error map table and emit both 'error.code' and 'legacy_status' in responses behind the proxy only

Pagination adaptor: legacy cursor parsers for both embeddings and rerank will include validation and expiry. If a legacy cursor references a retired shard, proxy will attempt a best-effort rebuild and return ERR_CURSOR_STALE with recovery instructions
Rate-limit bridge: ensure token bucket state is shared between legacy and unified rate-limiters during co-existence window
Telemetry: add compatibility-layer tags to traces and metrics (compat.layer=true, legacy_client=true/false)
Backwards compatibility tests: create a small harness that replays recorded legacy client traffic from production to verify parity before enabling canary
test_plan: Unit tests for error-mapping table and cursor translation logic
Integration tests that run legacy client mock against compat-proxy and compare responses to golden outputs generated by a legacy-compatible reference implementation
Property tests that assert no duplicate results and monotonic ordering across multiple pagination hops
Performance tests: measure median and p95 added latency at compatibility layer under 95th percentile request size distribution
Chaos tests: simulate shard retirements and verify ERR_CURSOR_STALE is returned with correct recovery token
End-to-end canary on staging with synthetic traffic mirroring top customer patterns. Gate on <0.5% correctness deltas and <10ms p95 latency regression
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Dev feature branch: implement modules and unit tests (ENG-48211)
Phase 1 - Staging integration: proxy enabled for internal traffic and synthetic replay (ENG-48212)
Phase 2 - Canary in prod: enable compat-proxy for 1% of legacy traffic and monitor SLOs for 48 hours
Phase 3 - Ramp: increase to 10% -> 50% with automated checkpoints. If error rate or correctness regression exceeds threshold, auto-rollback to previous config
Phase 4 - Full cutover: flip default routing and deprecate legacy endpoints on a scheduled date with 30-day dual-support window
Post-cutover: remove compat-proxy flags and clean up legacy parsing code after deprecation window
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboard: compat-layer/embeddings-rerank-parity showing request rate, latency p50/p95, error-rate broken down by error.code, legacy_status
Alert: compat.critical-correctness if mismatches between compat-proxy responses and golden reference exceed 0.2% over 30m
Alert: compat.latency-regression if p95 latency delta > 10ms vs baseline for >10m
SLO: compat success-rate >= 99.9% during ramp, with horizontal autoscaling thresholds set at 75% CPU for compat-proxy pods
Logging: include 'compat_context' in logs with truncated legacy_cursor and translated page_token to aid debugging
migration_playbook: Notify customers via changelog and release notes: explain page_token upgrade path and provide code snippets in SDKs
Provide client-side helper functions in SDKs (python/js/go) to convert legacy cursor -> page_token and handle ERR_CURSOR_STALE with retry guidance
Offer a compatibility-testing endpoint that mirrors a customer's production tenant for a 24h replay window to validate correctness
Step-by-step rollback instructions: disable compat-proxy flag, switch routing back to legacy endpoints, and purge transient page_token caches
Timeline: announce deprecation 60 days before final removal, with bi-weekly migration clinics with Solutions Eng
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased tail latency due to translation layer. Mitigation: lightweight proxy implementation in Rust with connection pooling and request coalescing
Risk: Cursor state staleness after shard rebalances. Mitigation: include server-side expiry and recovery tokens with best-effort rebuild path and clear error messaging
Risk: Clients relying on legacy numeric error codes break on string codes. Mitigation: include 'legacy_status' numeric field in compatibility responses for full parity
Risk: Rate-limit discrepancies during dual routing. Mitigation: shared token-bucket store and throttle coordination during ramp
